Subject: Acme POC — call recap & proposed 2-week trial plan

Thanks again for the call this morning, Sofia — great conversation and clear alignment on what success looks like. As promised, summary and proposed next steps for the 2-week POC: 

High-level objective:
- Validate Redwood inference for Acme's customer support summarization use case at 50 req/s (p95 latency < 200ms) while keeping inference cost under your target of $0.002/token.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
1) Latency: p95 < 200ms on staging traffic that matches your sample workload (avg seq len ~320 tokens)
2) Throughput: sustained 50 requests/sec for 30-minute window without queue growth
3) Quality: average ROUGE-L > 0.65 on your benchmark prompts and no major regressions vs baseline
4) Economics: per-token inference cost within target budget during the trial

POC plan & timeline (attached: redwood_poc_mop.pdf, acme_poc_milestones.xlsx):
- Week 0 (today — setup): grant staging API access, share sample logs, confirm test dataset and evaluation prompts
- Week 1: baseline runs + tuning (batching/quantization profile) and initial quality checks
- Week 2: scaled throughput tests, end-to-end integration smoke tests, final evaluation & handover

Owners/roles:
- Marissa Cole (Redwood) — POC owner, commercial point of contact
- Rishi Malhotra (Redwood) — SE, tuning and performance lead
- Neha Kapoor (Redwood CS) — integration & success metrics owner
- Sofia Alvarez / Tom Rogers (Acme) — staging access, dataset, and validation sign-off

Next steps (action items):
- Sofia/Tom: confirm success criteria above and provide staging API credentials and sample logs by Fri 8/7
- Acme: upload evaluation prompts to the shared Drive link (see related links)
- Redwood: schedule a short setup call with Rishi and Michael to configure the staging environment (30 min) — propose Tue 8/10 9:00am PT

If that all looks good I’ll send a calendar invite for the setup call and attach the evaluation template for your team to fill out.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
